newsitem.title: USA: USA Waste, WMX in Canadian deal.
newsitem.headline: USA Waste, WMX in Canadian deal.

text.p: USA Waste Services Inc's Canadian unit has executed a letter intent to buy most of the Canadian solid waste assets of Waste Management Inc, a unit of WMX Technologies Inc, the companies announced Friday.
In the deal, Canadian Waste Services Inc will pay US$186 million, consisting of $124 million in cash and US$62 million in USA Waste common stock, they said.
The transaction is expected to close by May 31, subject to Canadian regulatory approvals and the final negotiation and execution of a definitive sales agreement, they said.
When the deal is completed, USA Waste said it will have annualized revenues in Canada of about US$465 million from 13 landfills, 66 collection operations and 18 transfer stations.

The assets to be acquired by Canadian Waste are expected to bring in about US$124 million a year in revenues and include one landfill, 13 collection operations and three transfer stations servicing over 80,000 customers in the provinces of Alberta, Britisn Columbia, Ontario and Quebec.
At the same time, Waste Management's units will continue to own and operate divisions in Montreal and the Halton, Hamilton and Niagara areas in Canada.
USA Waste, based here, and WMX, based in Oak Brook, Ill., are both integrated waste management companies.
